title: Task 1 (Map Comparison): Redevelopment of Islip Town Center (2010 vs. 2025)
type: Task 1 Academic • Map Comparison (20m • Min 150 words)
visualHtml:
Map A: Islip Town Center (2010)
Map B: Islip Town Center (2025)
promptEn: The two maps above show the layout of Islip town center in 2010 and its redeveloped layout in 2025. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
promptMm: Cambridge IELTS Classic Map မေးခွန်းဖြစ်သည်။ ၂၀၁၀ နှင့် ၂၀၂၅ အကြား မြို့လယ်ခေါင် ပြောင်းလဲပုံကို နှိုင်းယှဉ်ရေးသားရမည်။ အဓိက ပြောင်းလဲမှုများ - (၁) အလယ်လမ်းမကြီးကို ကားမဝင်ရသော လူသွားလမ်း (pedestrianized street) အဖြစ် ပြောင်းလဲခြင်း၊ (၂) မြောက်ဘက် လယ်ကွင်းနေရာတွင် မြို့ပတ်လမ်းမကြီး (Ring Road) ဖောက်လုပ်ခြင်း၊ (၃) စက်ရုံဂိုဒေါင်ဟောင်းများကို ဖြိုချပြီး (demolished) Shopping Mall ဆောက်လုပ်ခြင်းတို့ ဖြစ်သည်။
outline:
1. Introduction: Paraphrase the prompt (illustrate the urban redevelopment of Islip between 2010 and 2025).
2. Overview: State that the town underwent extensive modernization, shifting from a rural-industrial settlement to a commercial and residential hub centered around a pedestrianized zone.
3. Body 1 (North & Central Road Changes): Describe the conversion of the northern countryside into a ring road, the pedestrianization of the main street, and the replacement of small shops and warehouses with a bus station and shopping mall.
4. Body 2 (Southern Sector Changes): Report the partial shrinkage of the town park and the construction of high-density apartment blocks.
template:
The two maps illustrate the urban transformation of Islip town center over a fifteen-year period from 2010 to 2025.

Overall, the town underwent comprehensive modernization, transitioning from a compact settlement with industrial warehouses into a commercial and residential hub built around a pedestrianized central thoroughfare.

Looking first at the northern and central sectors, the main road running from west to east was pedestrianized by 2025...

Turning to the area south of the central street, the public park was reduced in size...
modelEssay:
The two maps illustrate the urban transformation of Islip town center over a fifteen-year period between 2010 and 2025.

Overall, the town underwent comprehensive modernization, transitioning from a compact settlement bordered by farmland into a high-density commercial and residential hub centered around a pedestrianized thoroughfare.

Looking first at transport and commercial changes in the north, the countryside that bordered the town in 2010 was cleared to construct a dual-carriageway ring road to divert vehicular traffic. Consequently, the former main road bisecting the town center was pedestrianized. Immediately north of this walkway, the row of small shops in the northwest was replaced by a bus station and car park, while the old factory warehouses in the northeast were demolished to make way for a large shopping mall.

Turning to the southern sector, significant residential expansion occurred at the expense of green space. The town park in the southwest was reduced by nearly a third of its original area. In the southeast, the traditional terraced housing was redeveloped and expanded westward into a larger complex of modern apartment blocks adjacent to the remaining parkland.
modelMm:
၁။ Map Spatial Language: မြေပုံရေးသားရာတွင် 'bisecting the town center'၊ 'in the northwest'၊ 'adjacent to' စသည့် တည်နေရာပြ စကားလုံးများကို တိကျစွာ သုံးထားသည်။
၂။ Passive Voice Accuracy: မြို့ပြပြောင်းလဲမှုများသည် လူတို့ပြုလုပ်ခြင်း ဖြစ်သောကြောင့် 'was pedestrianized'၊ 'were demolished to make way for'၊ 'was reduced' စသဖြင့် Passive Voice ကို စနစ်တကျ သုံးထားသည်။

title: Task 1 (Process Diagram): Manufacture of Portland Cement
type: Task 1 Academic • Process Diagram (20m • Min 150 words)
visualHtml: Process Diagram: 5-Stage Cement Production Flow
promptEn: The diagram above illustrates the five-stage industrial process by which Portland cement is manufactured from raw materials. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features.
promptMm: Cambridge IELTS အကျော်ကြားဆုံး Process Diagram တစ်ခုဖြစ်သည်။ လူလုပ်လုပ်ငန်းစဉ် (Linear Man-made Process) ဖြစ်သောကြောင့် Present Simple Passive (is pulverized, is fed into, is heated) နှင့် အဆင့်ပြ Sequence Linkers (Initially, Subsequently, Following this, Finally) တို့ကို သုံးရမည်။
outline:
1. Introduction: Paraphrase the diagram title.
2. Overview: State that it is a linear, five-stage mechanical and thermal process beginning with raw limestone and clay and culminating in bagged cement.
3. Body 1 (Stages 1 to 3 - Crushing, Mixing & Heating): Describe how limestone and clay are pulverized in a crusher, blended in a mixer, and fed into a rotating kiln heated to 1,450°C.
4. Body 2 (Stages 4 to 5 - Grinding & Packaging): Explain how the resulting clinker is ground with gypsum and packed into sacks.
template:
The diagram illustrates the linear industrial process used to manufacture Portland cement from raw mineral inputs.

Overall, cement production comprises five sequential stages, beginning with the mechanical crushing of limestone and clay and concluding with the packaging of the finished powder into bags.

In the initial stage, raw limestone and clay are fed into a heavy mechanical crusher, where they are pulverized into a fine powder...
modelEssay:
The diagram illustrates the linear industrial process used to manufacture Portland cement from raw mineral inputs.

Overall, cement production comprises five sequential stages involving mechanical crushing, thermal chemical reaction, and fine milling, beginning with raw limestone and clay and concluding with the packaging of finished cement into sacks.

In the initial stage, raw limestone and clay are fed between two heavy rollers in a mechanical crusher, where they are pulverized into a fine powder. Subsequently, this powder is channeled into a cylindrical mixer to ensure a homogeneous blend before passing through a pipe into a rotating heater. As the drum rotates at an incline, intense heat of 1,450°C is applied from the opposite end, causing the mixture to fuse into small rocky nodules known as clinker.

Following the heating phase, the hot clinker is cooled and combined with a small proportion of gypsum to regulate setting time. This mixture then undergoes final milling between heavy grinding rollers until it forms a smooth grey powder. In the final stage, the completed Portland cement is distributed into standardized bags ready for commercial construction.
modelMm:
၁။ Process Verbs & Passive Voice: 'are fed between'၊ 'are pulverized into'၊ 'is channeled into'၊ 'undergoes final milling' စသည့် Process သီးသန့် ဝေါဟာရများကို သုံးထားသည်။
၂။ Overview Precision: အဆင့် ၅ ဆင့်ရှိကြောင်း၊ မည်သည့်အရာဖြင့် စတင်ပြီး မည်သည့်အရာဖြင့် အဆုံးသတ်ကြောင်း Overview တွင် တိကျစွာ ဖော်ပြထားသည်။

promptEn: The table above shows the percentage of total electricity generated from renewable sources in four countries between 2010 and 2025. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
promptMm: အချိန်ကာလ အပြောင်းအလဲပါသော Dynamic Table မေးခွန်းဖြစ်သည်။ နိုင်ငံအားလုံးတွင် ပြန်လည်ပြည့်ဖြိုးမြဲစွမ်းအင် သုံးစွဲမှု မြင့်တက်လာပြီး Norway က အမြင့်ဆုံးဖြစ်ကာ Germany နှင့် Australia က တိုးတက်မှုနှုန်း အမြန်ဆုံးဖြစ်ကြောင်း Overview တွင် ခြုံငုံပြရမည်။
outline:
1. Introduction: Paraphrase table description.
2. Overview: Upward trajectory in all four nations; Norway led throughout, while Germany and Australia achieved the steepest proportional surges.
3. Body 1 (Norway & Brazil): High initial baselines (65% and 48%) with moderate growth.
4. Body 2 (Germany & Australia): Low baselines but rapid expansion (Germany more than tripled to 54%; Australia quadrupled to 36%).
template:
The table compares the proportion of total electricity derived from renewable sources across four nations at five-year intervals between 2010 and 2025.

Overall, renewable electricity generation followed an upward trajectory in all four countries over the fifteen-year timeframe. While Norway consistently maintained the highest share, Germany and Australia recorded the most pronounced proportional surges.

Looking first at the nations with high initial baselines...
modelEssay:
The table compares the proportion of total electricity generated from renewable sources across Norway, Brazil, Germany, and Australia at five-year intervals from 2010 to 2025.

Overall, renewable electricity output followed an upward trajectory across all four nations over the fifteen-year period. While Norway consistently maintained the highest reliance on clean energy, Germany and Australia recorded the most dramatic proportional surges, significantly narrowing the initial disparity.

Looking first at the nations with high initial baselines, Norway generated 65.0% of its power from renewables in 2010 and experienced a steady climb to reach 74.0% by 2025. Brazil began in second place at 48.0% in 2010; albeit experiencing a slight dip to 46.1% in 2015, its renewable share recovered to finish at 56.0% in 2025.

By contrast, Germany and Australia started from considerably lower figures but achieved rapid growth. Germany's renewable share more than tripled from 17.0% in 2010 to 54.0% in 2025, nearly matching Brazil's final figure. Similarly, Australia quadrupled its renewable electricity proportion over the timeframe, rising from a modest 9.0% in 2010 to 36.0% in 2025.
modelMm: ၁။ Proportional Comparisons: ကိန်းဂဏန်းများကို ရိုးရိုးမရေးဘဲ 'more than tripled' (သုံးဆကျော် တက်လာသည်)၊ 'quadrupled' (လေးဆ တက်လာသည်) ဟု နှိုင်းယှဉ်ပြထားသောကြောင့် Task Achievement Band 8.5 ရရှိစေသည်။

title: Task 2 (Opinion): Public Transport Subsidies vs. Highway Expansion
promptEn: Some people believe that governments should invest primarily in expanding highways and road networks, while others argue that funding should be directed toward subsidizing and improving public transportation. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
promptMm: အစိုးရသည် အဝေးပြေးလမ်းနှင့် ကားလမ်းချဲ့ထွင်ခြင်းထက် အများပြည်သူ သယ်ယူပို့ဆောင်ရေး (ရထား၊ ဘတ်စ်ကား) အဆင့်မြှင့်တင်ရေးနှင့် ထောက်ပံ့ကြေးပေးရေးတွင်သာ အဓိက သုံးစွဲသင့်သည်ဟူသော အဆိုကို မည်သည့်အတိုင်းအတာအထိ သဘောတူ/မတူသနည်း။
outline:
1. Introduction: Paraphrase prompt + Clear Thesis (Maintain existing highways, but prioritize public transit).
2. Body 1 (Concession & Refutation on Roads): Rural roads are needed for freight, yet urban highway expansion induces private car demand and exacerbates congestion.
3. Body 2 (Public Transit Advantages): Subsidizing rail and electric buses mitigates emissions and narrows socioeconomic disparity.
4. Conclusion: Restate thesis clearly.
template:
It is frequently debated whether state budgets should prioritize the expansion of vehicular road networks or the enhancement of mass transit systems. While maintaining existing highways is undeniably necessary, I firmly believe that governments should predominantly allocate resources toward subsidizing public transportation.

Granted, well-maintained road infrastructure remains vital for...

By contrast, directing capital toward mass transit offers a sustainable solution...
modelEssay:
It is frequently debated whether municipal budgets should prioritize the expansion of vehicular road networks or the enhancement of mass transit systems. While maintaining existing highways is undeniably necessary for commercial freight, I firmly believe that governments should predominantly allocate funds toward subsidizing and modernizing public transportation.

Granted, well-maintained road infrastructure remains vital for rural connectivity and supply chain logistics. In regions where population density is too low to justify underground rail networks, highways serve as the primary economic artery. Nevertheless, relying on road expansion to solve urban traffic congestion is fundamentally flawed. Empirical urban planning research demonstrates that widening highways merely encourages more citizens to purchase private vehicles, which ultimately exacerbates traffic bottlenecks and atmospheric pollution.

By contrast, directing capital toward mass transit offers a sustainable solution to both environmental and social challenges. High-capacity rail and electric bus networks drastically mitigate per-capita carbon emissions, helping cities avert catastrophic air quality deterioration. Furthermore, affordable public transit narrows socioeconomic disparity by allowing lower-income commuters to access employment opportunities in central business districts without bearing the prohibitive cost of car ownership.

In conclusion, although basic highway maintenance cannot be ignored, prioritizing public transportation is indispensable for fostering equitable economic growth and environmental sustainability.
modelMm: ၁။ Concession Paragraphing: Body 1 တွင် 'Granted, ... Nevertheless, ...' ပုံစံဖြင့် တစ်ဖက်အမြင်ကို အသိအမှတ်ပြုပြီးမှ ခိုင်မာသော အချက်အလက်ဖြင့် ပြန်လည်ချေပထားသည်။

title: Task 2 (Discussion): Remote Work & Workplace Collaboration
promptEn: Some people think that the rise of remote working benefits both employees and the environment. Others argue that working from home isolates individuals and weakens workplace collaboration. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
promptMm: အိမ်မှအလုပ်လုပ်ခြင်း (Remote work) ၏ ကောင်းကျိုးနှင့် ဆိုးကျိုး အမြင်နှစ်ဖက်လုံးကို ဆွေးနွေးပြီး သင်၏ကိုယ်ပိုင်အမြင် (Hybrid model က အကောင်းဆုံးဖြစ်ကြောင်း) ကို ဖော်ပြပါ။
outline:
1. Introduction: Introduce the paradigm shift + State both views + Thesis (Hybrid model).
2. Body 1 (Benefits): Eliminates commuting, alleviates stress, and cuts rush-hour emissions.
3. Body 2 (Drawbacks): Encourages a sedentary routine and proves detrimental to junior mentorship.
4. Conclusion: Recommend a structured hybrid schedule.
template:
The proliferation of cloud technology has triggered a fundamental paradigm shift in employment, making remote work increasingly ubiquitous. While proponents celebrate telecommuting for reducing emissions, critics contend that it erodes team cohesion. In my view, a structured hybrid arrangement maximizes the benefits of both systems.

On the one hand, eliminating the daily commute...

On the other hand, abolishing physical offices altogether can be detrimental...
modelEssay:
The proliferation of cloud technology has triggered a fundamental paradigm shift in employment, making remote work increasingly ubiquitous. While proponents celebrate telecommuting for reducing emissions and improving work-life balance, critics contend that it erodes team cohesion. In my view, although exclusively working from home carries social drawbacks, a structured hybrid arrangement maximizes the benefits of both systems.

On the one hand, eliminating the daily commute yields substantial advantages for both workers and the ecosystem. In major metropolises, employees spend hours trapped in congested traffic, which heightens cortisol levels and diminishes productivity. Allowing staff to work as autonomous professionals from home alleviates occupational stress and reduces rush-hour carbon emissions. Moreover, companies can downsize expensive commercial real estate and redirect capital toward innovation.

On the other hand, abolishing physical offices altogether can be detrimental to organizational culture and mental well-being. Junior employees rely heavily on informal face-to-face interactions to assimilate workplace norms and receive mentorship. Furthermore, full-time telecommuters frequently slip into a sedentary routine, blurring the boundary between domestic rest and professional obligation, which can exacerbate feelings of isolation.

In conclusion, while unrestricted remote work risks alienating employees, adopting a flexible hybrid schedule allows organizations to cultivate teamwork while preserving environmental and personal well-being.
modelMm: ၁။ Balanced Discussion: On the one hand... On the other hand... ကို သုံး၍ အမြင်နှစ်ဖက်လုံးကို အလေးချိန်တူညီစွာ ဆွေးနွေးထားသည်။

title: Task 2 (Problem & Solution): Youth Unemployment & Academic Curricula
promptEn: In many countries, an increasing number of university graduates struggle to find employment in their chosen fields. What are the primary causes of this phenomenon, and what measures can universities and governments take to address it?
promptMm: တက္ကသိုလ်ဘွဲ့ရ လူငယ်များ အလုပ်အကိုင်ရှာဖွေရန် ခက်ခဲနေသည့် အဓိကအကြောင်းရင်းများ (Causes) နှင့် တက္ကသိုလ်များ၊ အစိုးရများက ဖြေရှင်းနိုင်မည့် နည်းလမ်းများ (Solutions) ကို ဆွေးနွေးပါ။
outline:
1. Introduction: Paraphrase issue + State that outdated curricula and automation are key causes, solvable via reform.
2. Body 1 (Causes): Theoretical pedagogy lags behind industry needs, while AI renders routine entry-level roles obsolete.
3. Body 2 (Solutions): Overhaul the curriculum with internships and subsidize graduate apprenticeships.
4. Conclusion: Summarize causes and remedies.
template:
Across the globe, a growing proportion of tertiary graduates face severe difficulties securing relevant employment. This predicament stems primarily from a mismatch between academic curricula and labor market demands, but it can be effectively alleviated through coordinated reforms.

The foremost cause of graduate underemployment is that traditional university pedagogy...

To counter these challenges, tertiary institutions and policymakers must implement targeted interventions...
modelEssay:
Across the globe, a growing proportion of tertiary graduates face severe difficulties securing relevant employment. This predicament stems from a mismatch between traditional academic curricula and rapidly evolving labor markets, but it can be effectively alleviated through coordinated educational and governmental reforms.

The foremost cause of graduate underemployment is that university pedagogy often prioritizes abstract theory over practical competency. Many faculties continue to teach outdated frameworks that have been rendered obsolete by technological disruption. Simultaneously, enterprises increasingly automate routine entry-level tasks in accounting, marketing, and administration, shrinking the pool of junior positions traditionally reserved for fresh graduates.

To counter these challenges, tertiary institutions and policymakers must implement targeted interventions. First, universities should overhaul their curriculum in partnership with industry leaders, integrating mandatory internships so students cultivate indispensable problem-solving and digital skills before graduation. Second, governments ought to subsidize vocational retraining and offer tax incentives to corporations that establish structured graduate apprenticeship programs.

In conclusion, although technological shifts and archaic degree programs have intensified youth unemployment, aligning higher education with real-world industry requirements can restore viable career pathways for young professionals.
modelMm: ၁။ Direct Cause-Solution Alignment: Body 1 တွင် ဖော်ပြခဲ့သော ပြဿနာအကြောင်းရင်း ၂ ခုကို Body 2 တွင် တိုက်ရိုက်ဖြေရှင်းပေးသည့် နည်းလမ်း ၂ ခုဖြင့် အချိတ်အဆက်မိမိ ရေးသားထားသည်။

title: Task 2 (Crime & Law): Prison Punishment vs. Rehabilitation
promptEn: Some people believe that fixed prison sentences are the most effective way to reduce crime, while others argue that education and vocational rehabilitation programs inside prisons are far more beneficial. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
promptMm: မှုခင်းလျှော့ချရာတွင် ထောင်ဒဏ်ချမှတ်ခြင်း (Incarceration/Deterrent) နှင့် အကျဉ်းထောင်တွင်း ပညာပေး ပြန်လည်ထူထောင်ခြင်း (Rehabilitation) အမြင်နှစ်ဖက်ကို ဆွေးနွေးပြီး ကိုယ်ပိုင်အမြင်ကို ဖော်ပြပါ။
outline:
1. Introduction: Contrast punitive incarceration with rehabilitative justice + Thesis (Incarceration is needed for violent offenders, but rehabilitation is vital to curb recidivism).
2. Body 1 (Punishment as Deterrent): Strict sentences act as a deterrent and protect society from violent criminals.
3. Body 2 (Why Rehabilitation Works Better Long-Term): Most non-violent crimes stem from poverty and lack of skills; vocational training helps rehabilitate inmates and lowers recidivism.
4. Conclusion: Balance public safety with rehabilitative reform.
template:
Criminologists and policymakers have long debated whether punitive incarceration or prisoner rehabilitation is more effective at curbing crime. While stringent prison sentences are necessary to incapacitate violent offenders, I contend that educational and vocational rehabilitation is far more effective at reducing long-term recidivism.

On the one hand, proponents of strict custodial sentences argue that prison serves as a vital deterrent...
modelEssay:
Criminologists and policymakers have long debated whether punitive incarceration or prisoner reform is more effective at curbing crime. While stringent prison sentences are necessary to incapacitate violent offenders, I contend that educational and vocational programs are far more effective at reducing long-term recidivism.

On the one hand, proponents of mandatory custodial sentences argue that the prospect of losing one's liberty acts as a powerful deterrent to potential lawbreakers. Furthermore, isolating dangerous individuals protects law-abiding citizens from immediate harm. However, imprisonment alone rarely addresses the root causes of criminality. When inmates spend years in idle confinement, they often become further marginalized from mainstream society and struggle to secure lawful employment upon release.

On the other hand, structured initiatives designed to rehabilitate offenders tackle the socioeconomic factors that stem from poverty and educational deprivation. Providing inmates with literacy classes, psychological counseling, and trade apprenticeships equips them with marketable skills. Empirical studies from Scandinavian correctional systems demonstrate that prisoners who complete vocational training exhibit dramatically lower rates of recidivism than those subjected to purely punitive detention.

In conclusion, although custodial sentences remain essential for violent crimes, prioritizing prisoner rehabilitation is the most sustainable strategy to reintegrate former offenders and foster safer communities.
modelMm: ၁။ Topic-Specific Lexicon: Crime မေးခွန်းအတွက် အမှတ်အမြင့်ဆုံးရစေသော deterrent, rehabilitate, recidivism, custodial sentences, law-abiding citizens တို့ကို သဘာဝကျကျ သုံးထားသည်။

title: Task 2 (Two-Part Question): Fast Fashion & Consumer Culture
type: Task 2 • Two-Part Direct Question (40m • Min 250 words)
promptEn: In many societies today, people purchase new clothing and consumer goods far more frequently than in the past, often discarding items after only a few uses. Why has this throwaway culture developed? Do you think this is a positive or negative development?

modelEssay:
Contemporary society is increasingly characterized by the rapid purchase and disposal of apparel and consumer electronics. This throwaway mentality is predominantly driven by low-cost global manufacturing and digital marketing, and I view it as an overwhelmingly negative development due to its severe ecological toll.

Two primary factors explain the rise of hyper-consumption. First, automated supply chains and synthetic textiles have drastically reduced production costs, enabling 'fast fashion' brands to sell garments at impulse-buy prices. Second, social media algorithms constantly expose users to ephemeral micro-trends and celebrity endorsements. This digital environment fuels ostentatious consumption, pressuring young adults to continually update their wardrobes to project social status online.

Although the retail sector generates short-term commercial revenue, the consequences of this throwaway culture are catastrophic. Millions of tons of non-biodegradable synthetic clothing proliferate in landfills and incinerators each year. Furthermore, textile dyeing and cotton cultivation deplete freshwater aquifers and accelerate chemical soil degradation in developing nations. On a psychological level, chasing fleeting material trends traps consumers in a cycle of financial debt and dissatisfaction.

In conclusion, while cheap manufacturing and relentless advertising have normalized disposable consumption, this trend inflicts irreparable harm on both global ecosystems and financial well-being.

In 2000, Country A had the highest rate of access at around 40 percent, while Country B and Country C were significantly lower, at approximately 15 and 10 percent respectively. Country A's figure rose steadily to reach nearly 90 percent by 2020.

Country B experienced the most dramatic growth. Its rate climbed sharply after 2005, and by 2015 it had overtaken Country A's early figure. By the end of the period, it stood at roughly 85 percent, just below Country A.

Country C started from the lowest base but increased at a more gradual pace. Its growth accelerated slightly after 2010, and it ended the period at around 70 percent, the lowest of the three.

title: Has Technology Made People Less Social?
modelEssay:
It is often claimed that modern technology has weakened human relationships, as people now spend more time communicating through screens than face to face. While this concern is understandable, I believe that technology has not reduced sociability; rather, it has changed the way people form and maintain their connections.

One reason for this view is that digital communication can make it easier to stay in touch with family and friends who live far away. Video calls and messaging applications allow people to share daily experiences that would otherwise be lost. In addition, online communities have enabled individuals with rare interests or health conditions to find others who understand them, something that was difficult in the past.

However, it would be unrealistic to deny that technology can have negative effects. When people are constantly checking their phones, they may give less attention to those sitting beside them. Excessive online interaction can also replace deeper conversations, leaving some individuals feeling isolated despite having hundreds of contacts.

On balance, the problem lies less in technology itself than in how it is used. Schools and families can encourage young people to set limits on screen time and to prioritize face-to-face activities. Such habits can ensure that digital tools support rather than replace human connection.

In conclusion, although technology can weaken social bonds when used carelessly, I believe it has largely expanded opportunities for connection.
promptEn: Some people believe that technology has made people less social. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

title: Space Exploration vs. Solving Problems on Earth
modelEssay:
Space exploration has long fascinated scientists and the public alike, yet it attracts significant public funding while many urgent problems remain unsolved on Earth. Some people argue that governments should prioritize space programs, whereas others insist that resources should be directed toward issues such as poverty and healthcare. This essay will consider both views before offering my opinion.

Supporters of space exploration point out that it has produced practical benefits that affect everyday life. Satellite navigation, weather forecasting, and medical imaging technologies all have roots in research connected to space missions. Moreover, exploration encourages scientific education and inspires young people to pursue careers in engineering and science.

On the other hand, critics contend that the cost of major space missions is difficult to justify when millions of people lack clean water, adequate food, or basic medical care. From this perspective, even a small share of a space budget could make a considerable difference to health or education programs on Earth.

In my view, governments should not treat these priorities as mutually exclusive. Space research should continue, but it should be funded at a level that does not reduce spending on essential services. Private investment and international cooperation can also share the financial burden.

In conclusion, although space exploration brings valuable benefits, the needs of people on Earth should remain the first priority of public spending.
type: Task 2 · Discussion (Both Views & Opinion) (40m • Min 250 words)
promptEn: Some people think governments should spend money on space exploration. Others believe that money should be spent on problems on Earth. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

title: Urban Traffic Congestion & Remote Work Models
modelEssay:
Traffic congestion has become a serious issue in many large cities, causing delays, pollution, and lost productivity. This essay will examine the main causes of the problem and suggest possible solutions.

There are several reasons why congestion is growing. First, the number of private vehicles has increased rapidly as incomes rise, and many people prefer cars for their convenience. Second, urban populations are expanding, which places greater demand on road networks that were designed decades ago. Finally, inadequate public transport in some areas leaves residents with few alternatives to driving.

Several measures could help to ease the situation. Governments could invest in reliable and affordable public transport, such as metro systems and frequent bus routes, to encourage people to leave their cars at home. Cities could also introduce congestion charges in the busiest districts, which would discourage unnecessary journeys. In addition, creating safe cycling lanes and pedestrian zones would give residents healthier and cheaper ways to travel.

In conclusion, congestion results from rising car ownership, urban growth, and limited transport choices. Addressing these causes through better public transport and well-planned incentives would make cities far more livable.

promptEn: Model B: Traffic congestion in cities is getting worse. What are the causes of this problem and what solutions can be suggested? (Also includes Model C: Working from Home advantages/disadvantages in commentary).

outline:
1. Introduction: State the traffic congestion problem (delays, pollution, lost productivity) and preview causes + solutions.
2. Body 1 (3 Clear Causes): Rising car ownership as incomes grow; expanding urban populations straining old road networks; inadequate public transit.
3. Body 2 (3 Concrete Solutions): Reliable/affordable metro & bus routes; congestion charges in busy districts; safe cycling lanes and pedestrian zones.
4. Conclusion: Summarize causes and solutions cleanly without introducing new arguments.

title: Weekly Leisure Hours (Bar Chart) & Plastic Bottle Recycling (Process)
modelEssay:
[MODEL D: BAR CHART]
The bar chart compares the average number of hours that adults in four countries spend on leisure activities each week. Overall, adults in Sweden devoted the most time to leisure, while those in Japan spent the least.

In Sweden, adults spent approximately 25 hours a week on leisure, the highest figure among the four nations. Canada was close behind, with roughly 22 hours, while the United States recorded a figure of around 20 hours.

By contrast, Japanese adults had the lowest average, at about 12 hours per week. This figure was significantly below that of the other countries, suggesting that work and other commitments take up a larger share of time in Japan.

[MODEL E: PROCESS DIAGRAM]
The diagram illustrates the stages involved in recycling plastic bottles into new products. Overall, the process consists of six main stages, from collection to manufacturing.

Initially, used bottles are collected from households and recycling centres. They are then transported to a sorting facility, where they are separated by colour and type. Following this, the bottles are washed to remove labels and dirt.

Next, the cleaned bottles are shredded into small flakes. These flakes are melted and formed into pellets, which are subsequently sold to manufacturers. Finally, the pellets are used to make new products such as clothing, containers, and packaging.
